expectations.text: Every finding in the review cites a specific path and line number.
expectations.evidence: Eight of nine findings open with path:line (Expressions.chibi:214, Statements.chibi:211-224, Expressions.chibi:390-397, Tree.chibi:118, docs/source-parser.md:19-20, Expressions.chibi:213-214, Expressions.chibi:383, source_parser_chibi.c:29-48). The '[TEST] test/language/syntax_corpus' finding heads with a directory but cites 'Body.chibi:2728 (36 links)' in its evidence. The commit-message NIT cites 'source_tokenizer_chibi.c:453-455', 'main.c:757' and 'Makefile:41'.

expectations.text: The review assesses whether the iterative else-if parsing preserves behavior of the recursive version (e.g., node structure, diagnostics) and cites the test or input that shows it.
expectations.evidence: 'I traced each rewrite against the parent, and the trees come out the same: New creates nodes in the same order, and the children and fields are the same. The node ranges match once the ParseIf fixup has run ... So the Tree-sitter differential is still a valid check.' Names the differential (SourceParserDiff.chibi driven by source_parser_chibi.c) as the check and the inputs that exercise chains: 'The longest else-if chain has 36 links (Body.chibi:2728)' and 'The syntax corpus contains a single else-if'. Weaker than tracing a concrete small chain (the without_skill review does), but it states the verdict and the test/input.

expectations.text: The review does not recommend defensive checks, compatibility shims, or splitting functions for length.
expectations.evidence: The only check proposed is '_Static_assert(sizeof PARSER_PATHS == sizeof PARSER_FILES, "one path per file")' as an alternative to merging parallel arrays: a compile-time assert of an invariant, which the repo's fail-fast rule favors, not a defensive runtime guard. The 'if (c.failed) { return -1; }' early return appears only conditionally under 'What I would measure' as a cost fix. Restoring ParseExpression/ParsePostfix/ParseArgument is about the depth limit, not length. No shims.

expectations.text: Every finding includes concrete evidence (a count, measurement, named caller/consumer or failing input), or the review states plainly that there are no substantive findings.
expectations.evidence: Most findings carry counts or inputs: DESIGN (51 call sites, frames 7 -> 3, ~70 -> ~48 at Body.chibi:3505), ParseIf SIMPLIFY ('Only 212 of about 6,100 if statements'), range-copy SIMPLIFY ('git grep ParseIndexValue finds one call site'), Opener TEST (invalid2.chibi.txt), corpus TEST (36, 17, 17, 15 links), commit-message NIT (313,206 > 262,144 bytes). But '[NIT] Expressions.chibi:213-214 — the comment about postfix forms sits above IsCallTarget' has no Evidence line at all: only 'Cost: read' and 'Fix: move the two lines'. No count, measurement, caller or input.

claims.claim: ParseExpression had 49 callers; 51 call sites now spell ParseBinary(c, n, OrPower).
claims.evidence: git grep -c at 2797053cb^: 'ParseExpression(c, n)' 17+13+19 = 49 lines in Declarations/Expressions/Statements. At 2797053cb: 'ParseBinary(c, n, OrPower)' 17+15+19 = 51.

claims.claim: The parser has 78 Expect call sites.
claims.evidence: git grep -c 'Expect(c, n,' at the commit: Declarations 37 + Expressions 14 + Statements 18 + Types 9 = 78.

claims.claim: Line 208 adds chained while it is still empty and NewNode sets end: -1 (Tree.chibi:50); since Add sets parent.end = child.end (Tree.chibi:75), every non-final link ends at -1 until the fixup, so the comment 'still ends where its own last child did' is wrong.
claims.evidence: Statements.chibi:207-208 'chained := New(n, "if_statement"); Add(n, current, chained, "alternative");'. Tree.chibi:50 NewNode has 'end: -1'; Tree.chibi:75 'n^[parent].end = n^[child].end;'. Later Adds to chained do not propagate to its parent, so non-final links hold -1.

claims.claim: SkipArgumentName always returns at least 1, so 'following > 0' at Expressions.chibi:383 is always true and the '0 when it is not one' doc is false.
claims.evidence: SkipArgumentName begins 'at += 1;' and only adds 2 in its loop, returning at; called with c.pos >= 0. The doc comment above it says '0 when it is not one.'

claims.claim: SCRIPT_CALL_DEPTH_LIMIT is 64 (src/language/semantic.h:11-12) and docs/language-friction.md:642-656 'Calls nest at most 64 deep' records two earlier walks turned into explicit stacks.
claims.evidence: semantic.h:11-12 at the commit: comment 'One language-wide recursion budget; authored source cannot override it.' and '#define SCRIPT_CALL_DEPTH_LIMIT 64'. language-friction.md has '## Calls nest at most 64 deep' naming the union-members walk and effect-analysis query restrictions.

claims.claim: At the parent Steps.chibi is 313,206 bytes, over the old 262,144-byte cap; invalid2's message would now end ' (to close the `(` at 4:10)'.
claims.evidence: git cat-file -s 2797053cb^:tools/compiler/package_compiler/Steps.chibi = 313206. invalid2.chibi.txt line 4 is '    x := (1 + 2', with '(' at column 10.

claims.claim: Depth at Body.chibi:3505 is about 70 frames at the parent and about 48 after the commit, leaving about 16 frames of headroom.
claims.evidence: Hand-counted estimate (stated as ±2 with the method in an appendix); not verifiable without running the differential. The review itself lists measuring actual call depth under 'What I would measure'.

suggestions.assertion: The review assesses whether the iterative else-if parsing preserves behavior of the recursive version (e.g., node structure, diagnostics) and cites the test or input that shows it.
suggestions.reason: Naming the differential as 'still a valid check' satisfies 'cites the test' without proving equivalence. Consider requiring a concrete traced input (e.g. a two- or three-link chain with its row order and end offsets) or an explicit note that the differential was or was not run.

No assertion covers whether the covering differential actually runs in CI. The without_skill review found that neither language-source-parser-chibi nor language-source-tokenizer-chibi is in any tools/test_policy.py GROUPS entry (verified); this review missed it. That is a substantive, verifiable outcome worth an assertion.

suggestions.assertion: Every finding includes concrete evidence (a count, measurement, named caller/consumer or failing input), or the review states plainly that there are no substantive findings.
suggestions.reason: This assertion fails both reviews on comment-placement nits. If nits are meant to be held to the same evidence bar, keep it; otherwise exempt NIT-level findings or require that nits be dropped when they have no evidence.

eval_feedback.overall: Central claims (no tree-shape bug, the fixup comment is wrong, following > 0 is dead) verify against the code. Fails only on one evidence-less NIT. The suite misses the CI-coverage gap that distinguishes the two reviews in the other direction.
